title: The Attention Mechanism
description: Break the sequence-to-sequence information bottleneck. Derive Queries, Keys, Values, and Scaled Dot-Product Attention.

slides.title: Breaking the Information Bottleneck 🎯
slides.content:
# The Flaw of Fixed Context Vectors

In classic Seq2Seq translation models (Bahdanau et al., 2014), an encoder compressed an entire 50-word sentence into a single fixed-size vector. This was like asking a translator to memorize a paragraph and translate it with closed eyes.

The **Attention Mechanism** allows the decoder to look back at *all original input words directly* at every generation step, focusing on the most relevant tokens dynamically!

slides.title: Queries, Keys, and Values 🔑
slides.content:
# The Retrieval Database Analogy

Modern Attention formulates relationships using database retrieval primitives:

$$\text{Attention}(\mathbf{Q}, \mathbf{K}, \mathbf{V}) = \text{Softmax}\left( \frac{\mathbf{Q} \mathbf{K}^T}{\sqrt{d_k}} \right) \mathbf{V}$$

| Tensor | Database Analogy | Semantic Role in Attention |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Query ($\mathbf{Q}$)** | Search query term entered in search bar | Represents what the current token is seeking |
| **Key ($\mathbf{K}$)** | Page titles / tags in the database index | Represents what each token in the sequence has to offer |
| **Value ($\mathbf{V}$)** | Full content of the matched documents | The actual semantic payload to be extracted and weighted |
| **Scaling Factor ($\frac{1}{\sqrt{d_k}}$)** | Normalizer | Prevents dot products from exploding in high dimensions, keeping Softmax gradients healthy |

quizData.question: Why is the dot product of Q and K divided by the square root of the key dimension (sqrt(d_k)) in scaled dot-product attention?

options.text: To convert the resulting matrix into RGB pixels
To prevent large dot product magnitudes from pushing the Softmax function into regions with tiny gradients
To enforce L1 regularization on attention weights
To eliminate the need for value vectors

quizData.explanation: For large d_k, dot products grow large in magnitude, driving Softmax into regions with near-zero gradients. Scaling stabilizes the gradients.

slides.title: Attention Matrix in NumPy 🐍
slides.content: Computing scaled dot-product attention from scratch:
slides.codeSnippet:
import numpy as np

def scaled_dot_product_attention(Q, K, V):
    d_k = Q.shape[-1]
    scores = np.dot(Q, K.T) / np.sqrt(d_k)
    # Softmax across rows
    exp_scores = np.exp(scores - np.max(scores, axis=-1, keepdims=True))
    weights = exp_scores / np.sum(exp_scores, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
    return np.dot(weights, V), weights

Q = np.array([[1.0, 0.0], [0.0, 1.0]])
K = np.array([[1.0, 0.0], [0.0, 1.0]])
V = np.array([[10.0, 20.0], [30.0, 40.0]])

out, w = scaled_dot_product_attention(Q, K, V)
print('Attention Weights:\n', w.round(3))
print('Weighted Values:\n', out.round(3))

slides.title: AI Pro Tip: Self-Attention vs Cross-Attention 🚀
slides.content:
## Two Faces of Attention
* **Self-Attention:** Queries, Keys, and Values all originate from the *same* sequence (e.g. words in a sentence attending to other words in that sentence).
* **Cross-Attention:** Queries come from the decoder sequence, while Keys and Values come from the encoder sequence (used in translation and diffusion image conditioning)!
